chat.why: Exam questions (LSAT logic and reading, LogiQA, SAT reading, Gaokao English) answered with one MC letter fit the chat reasoning/MC mix (bbeh, mmlu_pro), but about 38% of the English files are math.

math_code.why: About 38% is math (1,000 MATH test problems with closed-form answers, 220 SAT-math and 254 AQuA-RAT multiple choice); the rest is verbal reasoning, and there is no code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

agieval.licence: MIT (repo); data also follows each source dataset's licence (JEC-QA part is non-commercial, but it is Chinese)
agieval.overlap: math.jsonl holds 1,000 problems that are all, verbatim, in the MATH test split (my check against the local MATH copy): the same pool the live Yugos math set samples from.
agieval.summary: Human exam questions (LSAT, SAT, LogiQA, AQuA-RAT, Gaokao English, MATH); the 10 English files hold 3,852 questions (my count), mostly 4-5 option multiple choice plus 1,000 MATH cloze problems. Useful as easy-to-medium reasoning/MC chat data; drop the MATH part (it overlaps the live math pool).
sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ruixiangcui/AGIEval/main/data/v1_1/ (10 English jsonl files + LICENSE, counted locally)

2.model: GPT-4o (AGIEval-en few-shot, as listed in the AGIEval README)

languages: en (English subsets used here; the repo also has Chinese Gaokao/JEC-QA/LogiQA-zh files)

chat.why: General assistant instructions graded by a GPT-4 Turbo judge against a GPT-4 Turbo reference output (win rate), with no correct answer to check.

math_code.why: different skill: open-ended instructions, only a few coding/math ones and no tests or closed answers

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

alpacaeval.summary: 805 short open-ended instructions (median ~25 tokens; from self-instruct, OASST, Koala, Vicuna, helpful-base), scored as win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo by an LLM judge. Main value for a router: per-instruction outputs and judge preferences for ~220 models (228 results folders; 223 rows in the AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard CSV, newest 2024 models), but no reference answers, so quality is relative, not right/wrong.

chat.why: Grade-school science multiple choice with one letter answer: an easy MC chat question, like the very easy private chat part (calibration row).

math_code.why: Some questions need light arithmetic or units, but no competition math or code (calibration row).

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

arc_challenge.results_where: https://huggingface.co/open-llm-leaderboard-old (7,055 details_* datasets, config harness_arc_challenge_25: per-sample 25-shot results of open-weight models, 2023-2024)
arc_challenge.summary: 2,590 four-option grade-school science questions (median ~58 tokens) with a letter answer. Good filler for the easy private chat part; per-question results for thousands of open models exist in the old Open LLM Leaderboard details.

chat.why: Very easy grade-school science multiple choice with a letter answer; same shape as easy MC chat but simpler than any public chat set.

math_code.why: different skill: science facts, almost no math and no code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

arc_easy.summary: 5,197 easy four-option grade-school science questions (median ~47 tokens). Fits only the very easy end of private chat; almost every model gets them right, so they teach the router 'send to the cheapest model'.

chat.why: Hard real user prompts (coding, math, creative writing) judged pairwise against a baseline model by GPT-4.1/Gemini-2.5, with no reference answer.

math_code.why: Two-thirds of prompts are coding (253) or math (247), but answers are open-ended and judged pairwise, not run against tests or checked as a closed answer.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

arenahard_v2.summary: 750 Chatbot Arena prompts (500 hard: 253 coding, 247 math; 250 creative writing; median ~71 tokens) scored as win rate vs o3-mini (hard) or Gemini 2.0 Flash (creative) by LLM judges. Per-prompt answers and judgments for 30 2024-25 models (o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5, Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3...) help a router learn relative quality, but there are no right/wrong answers.

chat.why: It is the live Yugos bbeh set: 23 hard reasoning-puzzle tasks with short exact-match answers.

math_code.why: Some tasks are arithmetic or symbolic (multistep arithmetic, time arithmetic, boolean expressions), but not competition math or code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

bbeh.licence: apache-2.0 (HF card); GitHub: code Apache 2.0, other materials CC-BY 4.0
bbeh.overlap: is the live Yugos bbeh set: only the questions outside the live sample can be used, and never for testing
bbeh.summary: 4,520 questions (200 per task, 120 for disambiguation QA; a 460-question mini set) from 23 hard reasoning tasks, median ~620 tokens, short exact answer. The 4,370 questions outside the live 150-question sample are ideal chat-public training data, but must never be used to test.
sources: /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/bbeh/BBEH__bbeh/bbeh_data.json (local copy, task counts and lengths measured)

chat.why: The same 23 reasoning-puzzle task family that bbeh was built from, with short exact or MC answers, but much easier and long saturated.

math_code.why: A few tasks are arithmetic or symbolic (multistep arithmetic, boolean expressions, Dyck), not competition math or code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

bbh.results_where: https://huggingface.co/open-llm-leaderboard (~4,500 *-details datasets; configs leaderboard_bbh_* cover 24 of the 27 subtasks in MC form, open-weight models 2024-2025)
bbh.summary: 6,511 questions over 27 subtasks (median ~46 tokens without few-shot examples; exact or MC answers). Easy cousin of bbeh, good for the easy private chat part, and Open LLM Leaderboard v2 gives per-question results for thousands of open models.
sources: /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/bbh (local copy, lengths and guess floor measured)

chat.why: Only the 900 English questions fit: four-option reading comprehension of a short web passage, an easy MC chat question; the other 121 variants are translations (Yugos is English only).

math_code.why: different skill: reading comprehension, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

belebele.summary: 900 distinct questions on 488 FLORES-200 passages (median ~160 tokens), translated into 122 language variants (109,800 rows); only the 900 English ones suit Yugos. Easy MC reading questions for the private chat part.
languages: 122 language variants; en (eng_Latn) is the usable one

chat.why: Yes/no questions about one Wikipedia paragraph: reading comprehension like hotpotqa but single-passage with a binary answer.

math_code.why: different skill: reading comprehension, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

boolq.results_where: https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/ (prefix classic/benchmark_output/runs/v0.1.0 to v0.3.0, boolq:* runs with per_instance_stats.json; 68 models, 2022-2023)
boolq.summary: 12,697 public yes/no questions (train 9,427 + validation 3,270) on a Wikipedia passage (median ~135 tokens). Easy reading questions for the private chat part; HELM Classic has per-instance results for 68 older models.

chat.why: Real user prompts with one human pairwise vote between two models and no reference answer; mostly single-turn (1.2 turns on average), 96 languages.

math_code.why: different skill: some user coding/math requests, but no tests or closed answers, only a human vote

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

chatbot_arena_conv.licence: user prompts CC-BY-4.0; model outputs CC-BY-NC-4.0
chatbot_arena_conv.summary: 33K Chatbot Arena conversations (Apr-Jun 2023, 20 models such as GPT-4, Claude-v1, Vicuna) each with one human vote between two answers. Gives pairwise preference labels per prompt (only one model pair per prompt, 2023 models), useful for preference-style routing but not for right/wrong quality.

chat.why: Short five-option everyday-commonsense multiple choice with a letter answer; MC shape like mmlu_pro but commonsense, not school subjects.

math_code.why: different skill: commonsense, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

commonsense_qa.summary: 12,102 five-option commonsense questions (median ~28 tokens); 10,962 have answers (test labels are blank). Easy MC filler for private chat; old and well trained on.
sources: /root/cic/sn34-yugos/research/benchmarks/catalog/commonsense_qa (local copy, lengths measured, test answerKey empty)

chat.why: Short free-form answers to questions about a passage, scored by F1 like hotpotqa, but each question is one turn of a ~16-question conversation that depends on earlier turns.

math_code.why: different skill: conversational reading comprehension, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: multi-turn but no tools

coqa.licence: other (per domain: CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia/literature, MSR-LA children's stories, RACE licence, Apache news)
coqa.summary: 116,630 public questions (108,647 train + 7,983 validation, my count) over 7,699 stories (~380 tokens) from five domains, asked as a conversation. Could be flattened into single questions with history for easy reading QA, but the conversational shape differs from Yugos.

chat.why: Read a paragraph and give a short answer (span, number or date) scored by EM/F1, like hotpotqa, but the skill is counting/adding/sorting over one passage.

math_code.why: Simple arithmetic over text facts, not competition math or code.

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

drop.results_where: https://huggingface.co/open-llm-leaderboard-old (details_* datasets, configs harness_drop_3 / harness_drop_0, for models evaluated while DROP was on the leaderboard in late 2023; count not checked)
drop.summary: 86,945 public questions (train 77,409 + validation 9,536 on 579 validation passages; median ~256 tokens) about NFL game reports and history articles needing discrete reasoning, short answers scored by F1. Good easy-to-medium reading-QA chat data; labels are noisy (top models plateau near 0.9 F1).

chat.why: Short natural-language logic deductions (premises, then is the conclusion True/False/Unknown) with a 3-way exact label, close to bbeh's deduction tasks.

math_code.why: different skill: formal logic in words (FOL annotations exist), no math answers or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools, one question with one answer

folio.questions_where: https://github.com/Yale-LILY/FOLIO (data/v0.0 train + validation; also gated HF yale-nlp/FOLIO; test set unreleased)
folio.summary: 1,430 expert-written logic problems (paper), of which train (1,004) and validation (204) are public; each is ~5 premises plus a conclusion (median ~85 tokens), label True/False/Unknown. Medium-hard logic reasoning for chat; small set.

chat.why: One-line factual questions graded by an LLM judge against reference answers, like simpleqa_verified, but many answers change over time and a quarter have false premises.

math_code.why: different skill: world knowledge, no math or code

agentic.why: different skill: no tools in the prompt (built for search-augmented answering)

freshqa.questions_where: https://github.com/freshllms/freshqa (per-version spreadsheets linked from the README)
freshqa.licence: Apache-2.0 (repository; no separate data licence stated)
freshqa.summary: 600 short questions (500 test + 100 dev; never-, slow-, fast-changing and false-premise, 125 each in test), answers refreshed weekly (version seen 2026-04-21), graded strict/relaxed by FreshEval. Close to simpleqa in shape, but fast-changing answers reward recent knowledge, so labels must be the dated version used.
